1 وَثُجَ , aor. يَوْثُجُ, inf. n. وَثَاجَةٌ; (S, K;) and ↓ اوثج , and ↓ استوثج ; (TA;) It (anything, S,) became dense; thick; compact. (S, K.) ―
-b2- وَثُجَ, aor. يَوْثُجُ, inf. n. وَثَاجَةٌ, He became abundant in flesh; or very fleshy: وَثُرَ, inf. n. وَثَارَةٌ signifying he became abundant in fat; or very fat: and both signify he became bulky, or big; or large in body, corpulent and fleshy. (AZ, S.) ―
-b3- وَثُجَ النَّبْتُ The herbage, or plants, became dense, thick, or compact, and tall.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
